_doc: The evening inauguration (Inauguration, scripts/systems/inauguration.gd; the scene is scripts/world/inauguration_scene.gd). When you end a day in a place with a work day, the pieces you put up that day and left standing are opened at dusk: the biggest group of them (pieces within `cluster` metres of each other), with the villagers placed around it, a speech, a ribbon and the crowd's reactions. A layout's "inauguration" block overrides any of this; with no `speaker` there is no ceremony. Lines: {what} is the pieces ("a bench and two lamps"), {What} the same with a capital, {place} the hangout's `at` or `place`, {noticed} the complaint a need met had in the paper, {n} the number of pieces, {piece} the single piece. `tall` is how many metres one piece sits above the lowest before the speech calls it tall, `many` how many pieces make a spree. The speech is one `open` line, one `body` line (the first that fits: need, own, art, tall, colour, many, single, plain) and one `close` line. `grade` is out of 10, in halves: base, plus `need` for each need met (up to need_max), `kind` for each kind of piece after the first (up to kind_max), `usable` when someone can use it, `colour` for a painted piece; above 10 it's `lode`.

need: For years you told me: “{noticed}” I listened.
own: On my own castle steps, no less. Generous of me.
Right outside my office. I insisted. Modestly.
art: Some will ask what it is for. That is how you know it's art.
Is it a seat? A sculpture? A warning? Yes.
tall: Taller than my expectations, nearly as tall as my ambitions.
From up there you can see the next election.
colour: Note the colour. I chose it. In a dream.
Such a colour! The province will be furious.
many: {n} pieces in one day! I carried most of them myself, in spirit.
single: A single {piece}. Less is more, and more is expensive.
plain: It stands. It is ours. Mostly mine.
Solid work. I inspected it from a safe distance.

close: My vision, of course. The Geometra held the ladder.
Designed by me, built by the Geometra, paid for by... let's not.
Remember this at the next election. Scissors!
